conclusion: Recycled gfx950 literal-FMA opcode slots require architecture-specific aliases and a reset of shared decoder overrides before every ISA selection.
decision: Keep gfx942/gfx950 fixups bounded to the documented primary slots and exercise mixed ISA selection order in a regression test.
invalidated_assumptions: A static decoder table can retain the previous ISA's recycled opcode mappings safely.
observation: The decoder test passes gfx950, gfx942, and gfx90a in sequence and verifies both literal-FMA aliases and restored legacy slots.
question_or_symptom: Why can a decoder pass one ISA test and still misdecode a later ISA in the same process?
